item.title: Older adult care policy implications derived from quality of life disparities and sociodemographic risk factors
item.description: INRODUCTION: Population aging is placing increasing pressure on healthcare and social welfare systems worldwide, yet empirical evidence on whether integrated care policies for older adults reduce quality-of-life inequalities and improve well-being remains limited. This study examines the effects of such policies, together with socioeconomic, healthcare-access, and demographic factors, on the quality of life of older adults across countries.

item.title: Explainable fine-grained feature enhancement framework for strawberry diagnostic decision making
item.description: As the number of smart agricultural automation systems increases, accurate disease diagnosis is essential to maximize production efficiency. However, early-stage symptoms of strawberry diseases (e.g., Tipburn, Phytophthora blight, and Fusarium wilt) often manifest as low-contrast micro-symptoms that are visually similar to the inherent complex texture of strawberry leaves, leading to high technical difficulties in achieving an accurate diagnosis. Furthermore, providing an explanation for the...

item.title: RNDC-Lab: a real-time calcium imaging-based adaptive neural decoding framework
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Real-time neural decoding is critical for precise neuromodulation, which is of increasing interest in the treatment of brain disorders. This paper presents RNDC-Lab, a computational framework for designing, optimizing, and experimenting with real-time, calcium imaging-based, end-to-end neural decoding systems.

item.title: Pressure-Assisted Drug Delivery Using High-Pressure Balloon Platform Improves Vascular Drug Penetration and Anti-Restenotic Effects
item.description: High-pressure drug-coated balloon (HP@DCB) angioplasty enhances vascular drug delivery by overcoming the limitations of passive diffusion-based conventional noncompliant DCB (NC@DCB) systems. We developed a dual-layer HP balloon catheter composed of an outer Nylon 12 layer and an inner Pebax 7233 layer, and evaluated its feasibility and therapeutic efficacy as a paclitaxel (PTX)-coated platform. Shellac-based PTX coating was uniformly applied to HP@DCB and NC@DCB, and coating thickness, drug...

item.title: Interfacial Water-Networks Regulate the Anodic Stability of Carbon Electrodes
item.description: Carbon-based materials are widely used in modern electrochemical technologies, yet their susceptibility to oxidation at positive electrode potentials poses a durability challenge. While this degradation has commonly been addressed through modification of the carbon material itself, the interfacial chemistry that activates carbon oxidation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the hydrogen-bonding (HB) network of interfacial water strongly influences anodic carbon stability. Operando...

item.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of an elite indica breeding line resolves the genomic architecture of drought-yield QTLs qDTY<sub>2.2</sub> and qDTY<sub>4.1</sub> in rice
item.description: Drought-yield quantitative trait loci (QTLs) qDTY(2.2) and qDTY(4.1) improve grain yield under reproductive-stage drought in rice (Oryza sativa L.), yet their genomic architecture remains poorly resolved in elite indica breeding backgrounds. We generated a chromosome-level assembly of IR87707-446-B-B-B (IR64-qDTY(2.2) + qDTY(4.1)), which carries both QTLs in the IR64 background, and delineated donor-derived introgressions using informative parental single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). item.title: Unanticipated intermediates during isopenicillin N synthase catalysis identified by time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser studies
item.description: Biosynthesis of penicillin and cephalosporin antibiotics involves the oxidation of the tripeptide δ-(l-α-aminoadipoyl)-l-cysteinyl-d-valine (ACV) to give the conformationally strained bicyclic penicillin ring system, as catalysed by the Fe(II)-dependent oxidase isopenicillin N synthase (IPNS). The structures of the precursors for the sequential β-lactam and thiazolidine ring forming steps in IPNS have remained elusive. Here we studied the reaction of anaerobic IPNS:Fe(II):ACV microcrystals with...

item.title: Lower lung donor PaO<sub>2</sub>/FiO<sub>2</sub> ratio correlates with early primary graft dysfunction, but does not impact overall survival after lung transplantation: a dual center study
item.description: Extended criteria donor lungs falling below the arbitrarily set PaO(2)/FiO(2) (PFR) threshold of 300 are frequently declined despite other acceptable parameters. This two-center retrospective analysis investigates whether donor PFR is a risk factor for outcomes after lung transplantation (LuTx). A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted at University Hospitals Leuven, Belgium and Motol University Hospital, Prague, Czech Republic including adult LuTx recipients from 2010 to 2022 (Leuven) and...

item.title: Operational margin of high-school tennis tournaments under heat constraints: a wet-bulb globe temperature-based scenario analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Tournament feasibility should be evaluated based on operational margins as well as the predefined operational feasibility threshold. Although the threshold was met on average in most scenarios, the magnitude of the operational margin varied among tournament conditions. Combining changes in tournament dates with timing adjustments resulted in the greatest increase in low-risk operational time and tournament feasibility among the scenarios examined.

item.title: Changes in rat intestinal motility and absorption following intestinal transplantation: an experimental study
item.description: Intestinal transplantation (ITx) is a life-saving procedure for patients with complicated intestinal failure. In the acute phase, allograft permeability increases primarily due to ischemia-reperfusion injury. However, long-term allograft physiology after transplantation remains poorly understood, particularly the impact of lost autonomous graft innervation. This study aims to evaluate post-ITx allograft motility and permeability using orally administered fluorescein-labeled dextrans...

item.title: Grief-related social media use and perceived social media support among bereaved students: associations with grief, mental health, and continuing bonds
item.description: CONCLUSION: The study contributes to the limited body of research on grief-related social media use among students. Professional and peer support providers can play a crucial role by exploring the needs and coping strategies of bereaved students who engage with or seek support through social media and promote healthy coping and positive mental health outcomes.

item.title: Development and quality evaluation of lyophilized plasma external quality assessment samples for coagulation testing in resource-limited settings
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that the candidate lyophilized plasma materials possess satisfactory homogeneity, refrigerated storage stability, and transport stability, supporting their potential use as locally produced EQA materials for coagulation testing and reducing cold-chain dependence in resource-limited settings.

item.title: Microbiological patterns of bacterial bloodstream infections and predictors of kidney dysfunction at a tertiary hospital in Zambia
item.description: CONCLUSION: kidney dysfunction at admission is highly prevalent among adults with BSIs at NTH and is independently associated with older age, pre-existing CKD, lower hemoglobin-to-RDW ratio, and thrombocytopenia. The predominance of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens highlights the importance of early renal assessment, risk stratification, and strengthened antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited settings.

item.title: Recent developments in paraffin wax- sand/ C₃H₈O₂-H₂O nanomaterial under LTNE conditions using Levenberg-Marquardt method
item.description: The sand-paraffin wax/C₃H₈O₂-H₂O nanomaterial model for local thermal non-equilibrium (LTNE) circumstances has significant potential in advanced thermal energy storage and heat transfer systems. It is especially relevant for latent heat thermal energy storage units, solar thermal collectors, building energy management, electronic cooling, and industrial heat recovery systems, where paraffin wax acts as a phase change material and sand improves thermal conductivity and structural stability. The...

item.title: Functional redundancy and synthetic haploinsufficiency among Arabidopsis ATP-citrate lyase genes
item.description: ATP-citrate lyase (ACL) catalyzes the formation of cytosolic acetyl-CoA, which is the precursor for the generation of a variety of metabolites that have significant roles in plant growth and development. In Arabidopsis thaliana, ACL is encoded by three ACLA and two ACLB genes. The genetic functions of these genes were characterized by using combinations of null alleles of each subunit-gene. Individual acla mutants and double mutants that retained only the functional ACLA1 or ACLA3 gene exhibited...

item.title: Berberine-fluconazole synergy against drug-resistant Candida albicans: association with disruption of the Ire1-mediated UPR pathway
item.description: CONCLUSION: The synergistic effect of BBR combined with FCZ is associated with ER stress pathway dysregulation and autophagy activation in C. albicans. This study provides a potential therapeutic strategy for azole-resistant candidiasis, while further investigations are required to elucidate the precise underlying molecular mechanisms.

item.title: Relative timelines for transition from a hospital ventilator to invasive home respiratory support after tracheostomy in infants with chronic respiratory failure
item.description: CONCLUSION: Infants with and without BPD had similar transition timelines after tracheostomy placement. The mode of home respiratory support significantly affected this timeline in this small cohort, providing important hypothesis-generating data to inform further research.

item.title: Association of social determinants of health and all-cause mortality among individuals across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic stages 0-4: a nationwide prospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Higher SDOH burden is associated with higher all-cause mortality among population with CKM syndrome. This study underscores the necessity of incorporating SDOH screening into the CKM syndrome management framework.

item.title: Genomic insights into multidrug and extensively drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from bloodstream infections at three Zambian tertiary hospitals
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This first genomic survey of K. pneumoniae in Zambia reveals extensive clonal diversity dominated by global high-risk lineages carrying plasmid-mediated ESBL and carbapenemase genes. The detection of XDR strains, particularly at UTH, underscores the urgent need to strengthen laboratory surveillance across all tertiary hospitals in Zambia and improve infection prevention programmes.

item.title: Oligopeptide-binding protein A is a potential target for combating Salmonella infection
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings identify OppA as a conserved Salmonella antigen and suggest that it may represent a promising target for the development of subcutaneous and oral vaccines against Salmonella.

item.title: Characterization of pulmonary bacterial composition in community-acquired pneumonia depending on sampling methods
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: 16S rRNA gene sequencing provides comprehensive detection of pulmonary microorganisms and offers added value in the microbiological diagnosis of CAP. The findings highlight the importance of using invasive specimens for accurate microbiome characterization and for detecting bacterial taxa not identified by routine microbiological methods.

item.title: Facial pruritus and stiffness as the initial manifestations of glycine receptor antibody-positive progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus: a case report and literature review
item.description: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM) is a rare and severe phenotype within stiff-person spectrum disorders (SPSD), frequently associated with glycine receptor antibodies (GlyR-Ab). Because typical rigidity and stimulus-sensitive spasms may be absent at disease onset, early diagnosis can be challenging. We report a 52-year-old man who presented with facial pruritus, facial stiffness, limited tongue protrusion, dysphagia, and left lower-limb pain. Early manifestations...

item.title: Temporal changes in dilated ascending aorta after transfemoral TAVR: a comparative analysis of bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valves
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, dilated ascending aortas exhibited slow intermediate-term expansion following transfemoral TAVR utilizing self-expanding valves, with comparable rates between BAV and TAV morphologies. These findings suggest that conservative management of concomitant ascending aortic dilatation may be a reasonable strategy in older TAVR candidates during intermediate-term follow-up, provided that strict blood pressure control and rigorous imaging surveillance are...

item.title: TCR clonotyping of paired blood and tonsillar T-follicular cells reveals the mixed origin of CD38<sup>high</sup> Tfrs
item.description: Circulating T follicular regulatory (cTfr) cells are measured as blood biomarkers after vaccination, in autoimmune disease (e.g., lupus, rheumatoid arthritis) and cancer immunotherapy, yet whether they originate from natural Tregs (yielding nTfr) or germinal center T follicular helper (GC Tfh) cells (yielding iTfr) remains unknown. item.title: Adverse reactions of immune checkpoint inhibitors combined with acetaminophen/non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs): a pharmacovigilance analysis of drug-drug interactions
item.description: CONCLUSION: Based on data from the FAERS, four systemic disorders were identified to be associated with drug-drug interactions (DDIs) resulting from the combined use of ICIs and APAP/NSAIDs. Further preclinical trials and well-designed, large-scale clinical studies are needed to explore the potential pharmacodynamic crosstalk, alterations in inflammatory pathway and changes in the tumor immune microenvironment induced by the co-administration of ICIs with APAP/NSAIDs. item.title: Population cellular kinetics and exposure-CSR analysis of CAR-T cells in Chinese patients with relapsed/refractory B-ALL
item.description: BACKGROUND: CD19-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells have demonstrated great efficacy in treating relapsed and refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). Despite the high objective response rate of CAR-T cell therapy, high-risk adverse event of cytokine-release syndrome occur unexpectedly.

item.title: A single anion exchange chromatography step enables scalable, high-yield purification of hepatitis B virus capsid virus-like particles
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) causes a significant global health burden. The HBV core (HBc) protein forms the HBV capsid and has a crucial role in the virus replication cycle. When expressed across different platforms, HBc can self-assemble into HBV-capsid-based virus-like particles (VLPs), with a wide range of applications in both fundamental and pharmaceutical research. Due to their ability to display or crosslink foreign antigens on the surface, HBc VLPs are used as vaccine antigens....

item.title: Rabies immunoglobulin utilization and delayed presentation following category III rabies exposure: a 10-year retrospective study in Hangzhou, China
item.description: CONCLUSION: RIG utilization was low and showed marked temporal variation during 2015-2024, and one third of patients presented more than 24 h after exposure. Both outcomes were concentrated among working-age adults and domestic exposure settings. These findings describe service utilization patterns and identify subgroups in which gaps in PEP delivery are concentrated; targeted risk communication and routine monitoring of RIG utilization and presentation timeliness are needed.

item.title: Sex-dependent transcriptional and imaging responses to metformin in young-adult mice with SuHx-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension
item.description: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disease characterised by pulmonary vascular remodelling, right ventricular (RV) pressure overload, and ventricular metabolic reprogramming. Metformin has been proposed as a candidate therapy for PAH on the basis on encouraging preclinical results, most of which have been obtained in rat models and in single-sex cohorts. Its preventive effects in mice and its dependence on biological sex remain incompletely characterised....

item.title: Genome-resolved metagenomics reveals potential biochemical capabilities of a microbial community in an industrial wastewater membrane bioreactor during performance deterioration and recovery
item.description: This study investigates the microbial community composition and biochemical capabilities within a membrane bioreactor (MBR) system treating industrial wastewater during two operational states: a period of marked performance deterioration and a subsequent early recovery phase. The MBR system experienced a prolonged decline in treatment performance, with Total Organic Carbon (TOC) removal efficiency decreasing from approximately 90% to approximately 70% and effluent Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD)...

item.title: Candidate molecular endotypes and dynamic risk prediction in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease: a systematic scoping review
item.description: CONCLUSION: The evidence supports an integrated map linking recurrent molecular programs to dynamic pulmonary risk. A calibrated clinical-imaging backbone, augmented by parsimonious molecular modules with incremental value and updated at prespecified landmarks, offers a practical framework for prospective endotype validation and treatment-aware prediction in anti-MDA5+ DM-ILD.

item.title: Whole-genome sequencing analysis of phylogenetic relationships and lineage diversity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Western Kenya
item.description: CONCLUSION: Western Kenya harbors genetically diverse and spatially MTBC population with distinct patterns of phylogenetic relatedness. These findings demonstrate the value of WGS for characterizing population structure and informing targeted TB control in high-burden settings.

item.title: Therapeutic alliance and predictive validity of reflective functioning in conjoint mentalization-based treatment for borderline personality disorder
item.description: CONCLUSION: The study demonstrates overall satisfactory levels of therapeutic alliance in an MBT program for BPD but also indicates specific alliance-related challenges in the group psychotherapy component. Initial level of RF may not affect the therapeutic alliance in MBT treatment.

item.title: Tumor-antigen-specific polyclonal antibodies suppress tumor growth and metastasis in heterogeneous solid tumors
item.description: CONCLUSION: By simultaneously engaging non-redundant tumor pathways and reshaping the tumor microenvironment, XON7 may overcome key resistance mechanisms of solid tumors.

item.title: Gut microbiome-driven longevity mechanisms in giant pandas: age-associated gut microbial shifts, functional pathways, and probiotic insights
item.description: Microbiome-mediated longevity mechanisms in conservation wildlife remain largely uncharacterized, particularly in species with specialized diets where host-microbe coevolution plays essential compensatory roles. We conducted cross-sectional metagenomic profiling of gut microbiota in 82 captive giant pandas (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) spanning juvenile, adult, and geriatric cohorts. item.title: Influence of yoga on the epigenetics of obesity: a study on its short- and medium-term benefits in the treatment of patients with severe/morbid obesity eligible for bariatric surgery
item.description: CONCLUSION: In patients with severe obesity preparing for bariatric surgery, a structured preoperative yoga program was associated with a significant baseline-adjusted reduction in plasma noradrenaline, consistent with reduced sympathetic activation during a demanding phase of care. No epigenetic changes were detected, suggesting that measurable methylation remodelling may require longer exposure, larger samples, or tissue-specific sampling. item.title: Macroscopic cerebral energy efficiency corresponds to neuron reorganization in awake and anesthetized mice
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Non-invasive imaging of brain function and energy supply is crucial for diagnosing and treating brain disorders. Conventional imaging struggles to capture altered relationships between energy supply and demand caused by brain diseases. A novel method, thus far only tested non-invasively in human subjects, is to calculate relative power (rPWR) and relative cost (rCST) to assess cerebral energy efficiency. However, whether rPWR/rCST tracks individual changes and relate to neural...

item.title: Food for thought: food availability alters crayfish perception of fear and safety in risky habitats
item.description: Recent evidence shows that prey behavior is mediated by information regarding predators, refuges, and possibly food. However, the ways in which these 3 factors influence prey behavior in tandem with one another is still largely unexplored. We exposed rusty crayfish (Faxonius rusticus) to largemouth bass (Micropterus nigricans) odors and quantified sheltering and foraging behaviors. We presented crayfish with shelters of varying quality in 2 spatial arrangements and changed the location of a food...

item.title: Sodium-dependent multivitamin transporter deficiency caused by novel SLC5A6 mutations: a clinical case and personalized mice model study
item.description: The SLC5A6 gene encodes the sodium-dependent multivitamin transporter (SMVT), which transports biotin, pantothenate, and lipoic acid. Mutations of the SLC5A6 gene result in a hereditary syndrome whose symptoms range from early-onset, life-threatening systemic disorder to relatively mild, late-onset motor neuropathy. We describe a clinical case of a patient with previously unknown compound heterozygous missense mutations R280W and P437Q in the SLC5A6 gene. The patient exhibited a severe metabolic...

item.title: Unraveling hair graying: insights into melanocyte biology and the aging process
item.description: Melanogenesis and pigmentation are crucial processes for normal skin and hair, and they are regulated by complex factors. Unlike epidermal pigmentation, follicular melanogenesis depends on cyclic replenishment from a bulge melanocyte stem cell reservoir, making its functional decline generally irreversible yet clinically reversible under rare conditions. Herein, we systematically review the core biological processes governing follicular pigmentation, including embryonic specification, niche...

item.title: Expanding the horizons of facial mimicry in chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes): new insights into diverse signal types and contexts
item.description: Facial mimicry (FM) is an evolved mechanism in social mammals that potentially fosters emotional and physical connections through the production of congruent facial signals. Most research on FM has primarily examined relaxed open-mouth facial displays in the context of play. However, if the primary function of FM is to enhance the accuracy of predicting others' behaviors, it stands to reason that FM would extend to various contexts and signal types. item.title: Accelerating metadata annotation in collaborative research centers: a hybrid AI workflow for biomedical entities
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The hybrid workflow achieved high author-verified precision with moderate recall, shifting effort from drafting to reviewing while maintaining schema compliance. As these metrics rely on author acceptance and response rates were modest, broader, multi-site validation is needed.

item.title: Privacy concerns regarding social risk screening and documentation in the electronic health record: a qualitative study of patients' perspectives
item.description: CONCLUSION: Social risk screening and documentation systems must address patients' privacy concerns, facilitate safe disclosure, and clarify how data are used. Empowering patients with greater control over social risk data may affirm privacy and improve acceptability.

item.title: Histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomic analysis identifies an ECM-associated stromal pattern in lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma with complementary proteomic and functional analyses
item.description: CONCLUSION: Histopathology-guided spatial analysis identified an ECM-enriched regional transcriptional pattern in the stromal compartment of the analyzed LGACC section. Complementary proteomic and functional findings suggest that collagen-associated remodeling may contribute to the migratory phenotype of ACC cells. CD44 represents a biologically plausible candidate associated with the collagen response, although its mechanistic role requires further validation.

item.title: Efficacy of endoscopic ultrasound-guided versus surgical gastrojejunostomy for malignant gastric outlet obstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: For the palliative management of MGOO, EUS-GJ showed no statistically significant difference in primary efficacy endpoints compared with SGJ, but it might be associated with faster recovery and improved safety.

item.title: Effects and safety of acupuncture on inflammatory biomarkers in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: The pooled data yielded lower average CRP and IL-6 estimates, but low-certainty evidence, substantial heterogeneity, and prediction intervals including no effect preclude inference of a consistent anti-inflammatory benefit. Findings for hs-CRP and TNF-α were inconclusive. Current studies cannot distinguish acupuncture-specific effects from non-specific or contextual effects, and evidence on cardiovascular events and safety remains limited. Further well-designed trials are needed.

item.title: Inbreeding and its genetic and evolutionary consequences in red tilapia (Oreochromis spp.)
item.description: Managing inbreeding and effective population sizes in closed nucleus populations, such as red tilapia (Oreochromis spp.), is crucial to preserve genetic diversity and enhance selection response. This study aimed to assess these parameters (inbreeding, effective population sizes, and genetic diversity) in a red tilapia population undergoing selection for increased harvest body weight since 2016. item.title: Mitogenome-based phylogeny and evolutionary insights into Salticidae (Araneae) with emphasis on gene order evolution and selective pressures
item.description: Salticidae (jumping spiders) is the most species-rich family within Araneae. Despite recent advances in phylogenomic studies, mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) evolution and its contribution to understanding phylogenetic relationships in Salticidae remain poorly characterized. Here, we present a mitochondrial phylogenomic analysis of 107 salticid species representing all seven recognized subfamilies. item.description: We synthesised a series of N²,N⁴-diaminoquinazoline derivatives, among which 3-[[4-(benzylamino)quinazolin-2-yl]amino]benzenesulfonamide (compound 5) exhibited potent phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitory activity. Increasing evidence suggests that PDE5 inhibition is a promising therapeutic strategy for peripheral vascular disease. item.title: Arboreal signals in the skeletal proportions of the Gorilla foot
item.description: Postcranial skeletal proportions in living apes have been linked to patterns of arboreal behaviors within and between populations, offering a comparative baseline for interpreting arboreal behavior in fossil hominoids. We quantified metatarsal and proximal phalangeal lengths across all five pedal rays in Gorilla, comparing western lowland gorillas (Gorilla gorilla gorilla), low- and high-elevation Grauer's gorillas (Gorilla beringei graueri), and two ecologically distinct mountain gorilla...

item.title: Bridging the Gap Between Photocatalytic Water Oxidation Half-Reaction and Stoichiometric Pure Water Splitting Over Ta<sub>3</sub>N<sub>5</sub> via Cocatalyst Engineering
item.description: Despite significant progress in photocatalytic half-reactions and photoelectrochemical water oxidation, achieving stable photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta(3)N(5) remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, the incompatibility of cocatalysts between alkaline photocatalytic water oxidation systems and pure water splitting is identified as a critical bottleneck, leading to serious N(2) generation through photocorrosion. item.title: Biodegradable and Non-Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil-Plant Systems
item.description: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non-biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co-occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta-analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species...

item.title: Shear Alignment Polymer Extrusion 3D Printing of High-Loading Nanocomposites With Long-Range Ordered Nanostructures
item.description: Additive manufacturing has long struggled to bridge nanoscale functionalities with complex macroscale geometries, particularly for nanocomposites with high nanofiller loadings and ordered structures. Herein, we report shear alignment polymer extrusion (SHAPE) three-dimensional (3D) printing, a strategy that uses high shear forces to align highly loaded nanomaterials (e.g., boron nitride (BN) nanosheets and carbon nanotubes) along defined directions in polymer matrices, enabling the scalable...

item.title: Reverse Micelles: The Gateway for Oral (Poly)Peptide Delivery
item.description: Reverse micelles (RM) have played a central role in biotechnology, yet their pharmaceutical use has been constrained by instability, high water content and non-biocompatible surfactants. Classical wet RM (wRM) contain a discrete aqueous core whose size and solubilization behavior are governed by surfactant packing, hydration level and physicochemical properties of the hydrophobic phase. Although these systems provided insights into nanoconfined environments, their sensitivity to dilution and...

item.title: Cesium Tin Iodide Perovskites Engineer the Sn<sup>4+</sup>/Sn<sup>2+</sup> Redox Reaction in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
item.description: Tin displays rich redox chemistry transitioning between metallic tin (Sn⁰), stannous (Sn^(2+)), and stannic (Sn^(4+)) states, among which the Sn^(4+)/Sn^(2+) couple offers the highest theoretical potential ( >0.14 V vs. SHE) whereas remaining unrealized in practical batteries. item.title: Characterization of the Trimeric TOM Complex by HS-AFM Single-Molecule Analysis
item.description: The translocase of the outer mitochondrial membrane (TOM) complex is the entry gate for mitochondrial proteins synthesized in the cytosol. item.title: Correlative 3D Electron Tomography and Nanobeam 4D-STEM Mapping of Orientation and Strain in Welded Silver Nanowires
item.description: A correlative analysis combining three-dimensional (3D) electron tomography and small convergence angle convergent-beam electron diffraction acquired in four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) mode is used to investigate the structure, crystallographic orientation, and strain distribution in thermally welded silver nanowire (AgNW) junctions. item.title: Investigating the TASK1 potassium channel in equine atrial myocardium as a potential treatment target for atrial fibrillation
item.description: CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: EqTASK1 channels are highly conserved with human orthologs and display pronounced atrial-predominant cardiac expression. In vivo TASK1 inhibition prolongs atrial refractoriness in horses, supporting TASK1 as a translational atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target in both human and veterinary medicine.

item.title: Interspecific Gene Flow and Potential Hybrid Breakdown in South Atlantic Sea Turtles
item.description: Interspecific hybridisation can play an important evolutionary role, generating new taxa or outbreeding depression, which can also lead to behavioural reproductive isolation through reinforcement. Still, there are few studies investigating how divergence time relates to hybridisation rates and its impact on introgression. item.title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO<sub>2</sub>
item.description: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO(2). We integrated regional tree-ring data with a peatland warming and CO(2) manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana, to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO(2). item.title: 2D Borophene Oxide Substrate for C<sub>2+</sub> Products Synthesis via CO<sub>2</sub> Electroreduction at Industrial Current Densities
item.description: The industrialization of electrochemical CO(2) reduction reaction for multi-carbon products synthesis is limited by HER competition, sluggish C─C coupling kinetics, and carbonate deposition. Through rational computational screening, we identify β-rhombohedral borophene oxide (β-rh. BO) as an ideal two-dimensional substrate to simultaneously overcome these bottlenecks. item.title: Ambulatory Episodic Hypertension in Parkinson's Disease With Orthostatic Hypotension
item.description: OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to determine whether ambulatory hypertensive episodes are associated with clinical outcomes in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) with neurogenic versus non-neurogenic orthostatic hypotension.

item.title: Association of frailty screening-based preventive care with long-term care certification rates among Japanese people aged 75 years and older: an interrupted time-series analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: The frailty screening-based preventive care initiative for older adults was associated with a reduction in LTC certification rates. These findings suggest the potential value of linking frailty screening with broad preventive guidance as a municipal approach to addressing population-level LTC need.

item.title: Suppressing Irreversible Interfacial Spatial Electron Transfer for High-Temperature 4.6 V LiCoO<sub>2</sub>
